Thunder Dome Creative Test SOP
Presented By Dana Example
FICTIONAL TRAINING MATERIAL FOR TESTS

What the Thunder Dome is
The Thunder Dome is a head-to-head creative test. You put several ad creatives in one ring, give them the same conditions, and let the numbers pick the winner.
The point is to stop guessing which hook works. Opinions do not win the Thunder Dome, cost per lead does.

The rules of a Thunder Dome test
Rule 1: Test between three and five creatives at a time. Fewer than three gives you no comparison. More than five spreads the budget too thin.
Rule 2: Every creative goes into the same ad set with the same audience. Do not change targeting during the test.
Rule 3: Give each creative an equal daily budget. A common starting point is twenty to thirty dollars per creative per day on the practice account.
Rule 4: Change only one variable between creatives. Test the hook, or the visual, or the offer line. Never all three at once.
Rule 5: Run the test for a minimum of seventy-two hours before you judge it.
Rule 6: A creative needs at least one thousand impressions before you can call it a loser.

The kill rule
Kill any creative whose cost per lead is more than two times your target cost per lead after it has spent one and a half times the target cost per lead.
If your target cost per lead is ten dollars, a creative that has spent fifteen dollars with zero leads gets switched off.
Do not kill a creative early because you dislike it. Kill it because the kill rule says so.

Picking the winner
The winner is the creative with the lowest cost per lead after seventy-two hours, as long as its click-through rate is at least one percent.
If two creatives are within ten percent of each other on cost per lead, pick the one with the better lead quality from the setter notes.
The winner graduates to the scaling campaign. The losers get archived, not deleted, so you keep the learnings.

After the Thunder Dome
Write down why you think the winner won. Was it the hook, the visual or the offer line?
Use that note to brief the next round. Each new Thunder Dome should test one new idea against the current champion.
Run a new Thunder Dome every two weeks so creative fatigue never catches you out.
Creative fatigue shows up as a rising cost per lead and a falling click-through rate on the same creative over seven days.
